# Feature — Enforce the post-deadline thrash gate at every local-dispatch entry; terminal in-request detour

Child of LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV. Implementation slice: after the deterministic tests
(C1) pin the mechanism, make the cancelled session's claim on the local gate end with
the cancellation — the thrash-cooldown gate engages for EVERY local dispatch attempt
(including paths that bypass provider.py's chain gate), the same request does not
re-dispatch local after the deadline detour, and any remaining lease is bounded
≤300 s.

## Target outcome

A local dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` stops holding the local
dispatch gate: no in-request local re-dispatch acquiring a fresh lease ~150 ms after
the release; the per-session thrash cooldown demonstrably engages at every local
dispatch entry; `local_prefill_in_flight` never outlives the dispatch it marks; every
remaining hold is bounded ≤300 s (parent AC1-AC3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1. Every path that can acquire a local dispatch lease consults the per-session
  thrash cooldown before acquisition — including direct local paths that bypass
  provider.py's chain gate (the shape C1's isolation test surfaced). A session whose
  cooldown is armed is refused (`routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`)
  with the chain falling to the next provider. C1's gate-engagement test goes green.
  Rollback knob `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 0` still disables the gate.
- AC2. The deadline detour is terminal for local within that request: a request-scoped
  marker set on `prefill_deadline_exceeded` prevents the same request from acquiring a
  fresh lease after release (the ~150 ms post-release fresh lease is impossible). C1's
  re-dispatch test goes green.
- AC3. After the cancellation the lease, `local_prefill_in_flight` marker are cleared
  BEFORE any retry, and the cancelled upstream prefill stream is closed (proven dead)
  so `_extend_prefill_lease` cannot re-extend from a stale marker (no
  `lease_extended_during_prefill ... in_flight=True` after release). C1's marker test
  goes green.
- AC4. Any remaining hold is bounded ≤300 s from its last progress for every
  acquisition path (deadline detour, same-session re-acquisition, active-expired
  sweep) without weakening the 180 s no-progress watchdog or the 10 s sweep cadence.
  C1's bound test goes green.
- AC5. Legitimate long prefills are unaffected: a live, progressing prefill keeps its
  lease (no-preemption same-session semantics preserved); first-byte latency stays
  inside `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`; a successful local first byte clears
  the cooldown per the recovery-fraction rule (parent constraints).
- AC6. Changed-scope test gate passes and the full suite stays green with the fix.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken: the prefill deadline (120 s) detour-not-kill backstop, the
  no-progress watchdog (180 s), the 10 s sweep, the thrash cooldown (600 s / rollback
  knob 0), no-preemption same-session lease re-acquisition for genuine in-flight
  prefills.
- Scope: do NOT absorb lease-fairness renewal caps (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0) — record any
  overlap as related work, keep that item's scope there.
- Fix the mechanism C1 identifies (bypass and/or arm-key mismatch); a renewal cap alone
  is insufficient if the gate remains unengaged (parent AC1 mandates an engaged gate).

## Risky assumptions

- The incident re-dispatch is a same-request/retry client pattern (pi/opencode retries
  on 503); the request-scoped marker must not block unrelated concurrent requests from
  the same session (the session cooldown covers those).
- Closing the upstream prefill stream is sufficient to prevent stale-marker
  re-extension (verify with C1's marker test).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a request-scoped post-deadline marker set in the `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
   path and checked at the lease-acquisition choke point; local is terminal for that
   request (chain falls to the next provider).
2. Consult the thrash cooldown at the single choke point every local dispatch passes
   (router.py `proxy_to_local` immediately before `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`) so
   direct bypass paths engage; keep the existing provider.py gate.
3. Harden the release path (deadline + measured-abort twins) so record + marker
   removal and upstream-stream close (bounded by `disconnect_cleanup_timeout`) complete
   before any retry can observe stale state.
4. Update code comments at the changed sites; keep the existing log vocabulary
   (`routing_skip_local`, `lease_released`, `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started`).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`proxy_to_local`, `prefill_deadline_exceeded` block)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_*`, `_extend_lease_during_prefill`)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (local branch + any direct dispatch paths C1 surfaces)
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` (harness extended by C1)
- Related: `proxy/proxy/ui.py` (`_dispatch_local_model_load` direct
  `srv.proxy_to_local`), per C1's cause comment
data.title: Enforce the post-deadline thrash gate at every local-dispatch entry; terminal in-request detour

# Load-normalise the AC3 denial check in the idle-admit measurement

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the AC3 `local_dispatch_denied` check normalised to
window load (per bypass/fallback event), so the measured `+9.3 %` per-hour
denial "increase" (window 2026-10-22 21:48 → 2026-10-23 21:48, ~2× busier than
the before window) is judged on a load-independent signal instead of a
confounded raw rate.

## Measured evidence (artifact `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `local_dispatch_denied` raw | 66.0 /h | 72.1 /h | **+9.3 %** (> 5 % band → fail) |
| `large_context_bypass` events | 1,790 | 3,702 | +107 % |
| Remote fallback events | 6,953 | 12,888 | +85 % |
| Denials per bypass+fallback event | 1,584/8,743 = 0.181 | 1,731/16,590 = 0.104 | −42 % |

The raw rate cannot distinguish "the override causes more denials" from "a 2×
heavier window produces proportionally more denials". The tool currently
implements only the raw per-hour rate (`scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`:
`denied_before_rate`/`denied_after_rate`, `_DENIED_TOLERANCE_PCT = 5.0`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` reports a load-normalised denial rate — denials per bypass+fallback event — alongside the existing per-hour rate, in both the AC3 check and the JSON/markdown output.
- The AC3 verdict uses the normalised rate for pass/fail (the raw per-hour rate remains reported), so a raw increase caused purely by higher load no longer fails the check; a genuine per-event increase still fails.
- Tests cover: the normalised-rate arithmetic against the exact window numbers above (fail → pass), a synthetic per-event denial increase that still fails the check, and backward compatibility of all existing JSON keys and exit codes.
- Re-running the tool `--window-closed` on the closed window records the AC3 verdict on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD next to the baselines table, with the normalised numbers and sample counts.
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` documents the normalised metric definition and why the raw per-hour rate is load-confounded.

## Key Files

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`

# tree_coverage AC extraction truncates hard-wrapped bullets (false coverage "stop")

Discovered from: LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — while planning that item, the shared
AC-coverage review reported every parent AC as uncovered with `recommendation:
"stop"`, even though the children (LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF, LP-0MVRCLPVI0057116)
clearly cover the scope.

## Root cause

`extract_acceptance_criteria()` in `skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` treats each
physical line as one AC. The project's descriptions hard-wrap AC bullets at
~80 columns, so a single bullet like "A ≥24 h post-deploy window is analysed
with `proxy-usage-analysis` and reports, next to the baselines above: ..." is
cut to its first fragment ("...and reports,"). Similarity matching against
child ACs (also wrapped) then scores 0.05–0.18, below the 0.2 auto-close
floor, and every AC is reported uncovered (coverage 0 %, recommendation
"stop"). Re-flowing the AC text into single lines restores full sentences but
the matcher still cannot see the mapping because both sides are truncated.

## Impact

- False `stop` results block stage advancement on wrapped items (LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD
  sat `intake_complete` while its measurement work was already recorded).
- Coverage % is meaningless (0 %) for well-maintained wrapped descriptions.
- Auditors/planners must manually re-verify coverage on every wrapped item.

## Acceptance criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria()` joins wrapped continuation lines of a bullet
  into a single AC entry instead of truncating at the first line (indented
  sub-list markers still excluded as before).
- A regression test covers a hard-wrapped multi-line AC bullet and asserts one
  complete AC is returned.
- Re-running coverage review on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD after the fix no longer
  reports all 5 parent ACs as uncovered (score movement is what matters, not
  a specific threshold).

## Key Files

- `skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` (agent infrastructure — do not edit without
  operator approval; the fix itself is a separate authorised change)
- `skills/plan/tests/`

Measured 2026-10-27 16:16 → 2026-10-28 15:55 (24h post-payload window) by the deterministic analysis CLI: the published prefill_eta_seconds does **not** predict real prefill duration for dispatches that ran.

Evidence: /home/rgardler/proxy-usage-reports/report.md — 'Local contention prediction vs reality' M3 table.
- Predicted (status_request polls): p50 = 91.6 s (n=10,618), p90 = 124.2 s
- Observed (llama-server prompt eval time): p50 = 2.4 s (n=901), p90 = 27.7 s
- Signed error (pred − obs): p50 +89.3 s (relative +3865%), p90 +96.5 s (relative +348%)
- Verdict: over_predicts (tolerance 25%)

Why it matters: the ETA is the cache-cold reference-prompt cost used by admissions and published to dispatchers (status_estimate, proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py). A dispatcher pacing on the published ETA will refuse work that would actually be served quickly — i.e. the signal over-refuses servable local work. The reference prompt appears systematically far larger than the median served prompt.

Open question for calibration: should the ETA be calibrated to the observed distribution (e.g. prompt-size-banded calibration), or relabelled as a worst-case bound, or budgeted per-request? See LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ / LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM for the calibration lineage.

Known limitation: llama-server eval lines carry no per-line timestamp, so the comparison is quantile-matched (p50/p90 of each distribution), not per-dispatch pairing (documented in REFERENCE.md Limitations).

## Problem

The dev-push full-suite gate can run the suite against the **main checkout's stale working tree** instead of the commit actually being pushed.

`implement.py finish` pushes from the main checkout (`repo_root` — see the `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, ...)` call sites in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, and the Step-5 comment "the pre-push hook measures the working tree (which is the main checkout at push time)"). It first fast-forwards the main checkout's `dev` to the new commit so the hook sees the updated files. When the main checkout is **dirty** (another agent's WIP, a concurrent finish, operator edits), that fast-forward is safe-skipped, and the push then runs `.githooks/pre-push` with `run_tests.py --scope full --project-root <main checkout>` — measuring the *old* tree, not the pushed commit.

## Evidence (2026-10-28, LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND)

- Main checkout dirty (8 unrelated paths) -> Step-5 fast-forward skipped; main checkout `dev` stayed at `7393ef14` while the push landed `11870e99`.
- The pre-push gate returned green in seconds (cache hit on the *main checkout's* git-state fingerprint); no full-suite cache entry was created for the pushed commit's clean fingerprint `afce15bd...`.
- `run_tests.py --summary` after the push reported `missing` for HEAD (expected when the main checkout is not the pushed commit) — the documented post-push verification signal for this gap.
- Verifying the pushed commit in a throwaway worktree (`run_tests.py --scope full --project-root <worktree>`) gave 6136 passed / 0 failed and wrote the missing cache entry, proving the commit was fine — but nothing in the normal flow had verified it.

## Why it matters

A commit can land on `dev` without the full suite ever running against its tree whenever any concurrent process leaves the main checkout dirty. The gate is the only full-suite enforcement point for dev/main, so this is a silent fail-open.

## Suggested direction (report only — framework files are out of scope for this item)

- When the Step-5 fast-forward is skipped, either (a) gate the pushed commit itself (e.g. pass the commit's project root / push from the worktree), or (b) fail closed with an actionable message; at minimum detect that the gate's git-state fingerprint is not the pushed commit and say so in the finish report.
- Related surface: `.githooks/pre-push` (`--project-root "$repo_root"`) and `mirror_suite_cache`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A finish whose main-checkout fast-forward is skipped either fails closed or gates the pushed commit itself; the finish report names which tree the gate verified.
- A regression test covers "dirty main checkout + skipped fast-forward" and asserts the pushed commit is the tree under test.

Discovered-from: LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND (surfaced during post-push verification of its dev push).
data.title: dev-push full-suite gate verifies a stale main checkout when the pre-push fast-forward is skipped

# Feature: `local-preferred` pin across every local-route exit

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 (preference vocabulary — canonical `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED`, alias normalisation) and LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ (capacity verdict feature, incl. its children LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB `local_capacity_verdict()` and LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6 wiring).

## Goal

A `local-preferred` request whose capacity verdict is `deferrable` is never handed to a non-local provider, whichever way the local route exits — admission refusal, lease denial, slot exhaustion, context/`resident_prefix` skip, stall, empty response or sibling-failure — on **both** dispatch cycles. This is today's `local-only` guarantee, expressed on the new canonical value and gated by the verdict instead of by the raw header value.

This slice is the *pin* half of the parent feature: it decides **whether** a non-local dispatch may happen. Deferral (queue-budget expiry → retryable 429) is LP child "deferral"; chain-level stripping of local on `too_large` and the promoted log line are LP child "too-large promotion"; the single per-request outcome line is LP child "routing-outcome line".

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
  - One request-scoped pin predicate (e.g. `_local_preference_pins_local(request, preference) -> bool`) returning `True` only when the resolved preference is the canonical pin-local constant **and** `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` is **not** `too_large`. `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / absent → `False`; `too_large` → `False` (the request must fall through, never be refused).
  - `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` (~:6686) — replace the raw `preference != _PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` comparison with the predicate, at **both** call sites (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` ~:10057, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` ~:10742). Docstring reworded from "local-only choke point" to "pin-local choke point" naming `local-preferred` (the alias is already normalised upstream, so one branch covers both wire values).
  - The admission-refusal comparison in `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (~:7130, `return ("refused_local_only", ...)`) uses the predicate, so a deferrable `local-preferred` request returns the existing refusal instead of `admission_reject` fall-through, while a `too_large` request keeps the `admission_reject` fall-through with **no** 429.
  - The remote-fallback / direct-guard comparison in the `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` free-slot path (~:11460 region, `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`) is audited and routed through the same predicate — no third hand-rolled comparison.
  - No new refusal construction: the refusal keeps coming from `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` / `_refusal_retry_timing()` unchanged (the body `verdict` field arrives with LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — extend `_EXIT_ROWS` coverage with a `local-preferred` parameterisation. Every row asserts its **own** outcome (no shared assertion):
  - deferrable-classified rows (`thrash_cooldown`, `router_skip_economic`, `router_skip_residency`, `router_skip_tenancy`, `queue_depth_cap`, `queue_wait_expiry`, `admission_guard_free_slot`, `quota_hard_stop`, `chain_cooldown`, `no_local_route`) → `calls == []`, 429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, header reason token and body `reason` agreeing;
  - too-large-classified rows (`router_skip_physical_cap` `context_too_large`, `entry_context_cap`) → `calls == ["remote"]`, 200, no refusal code (parent AC4 boundary; see AC4);
  - **post-dispatch exits** (parent AC1's "slot exhaustion, stall, empty response, sibling-failure"): new rows whose local dispatch *is* attempted once and then fails — slot exhaustion (`slot_info` / 409 lease-active), lease denial after the lease wait (`_lease_action == "fallback"` / `"refused_local_only"`), GPU OOM, `model_loading`, local error status, empty local response (`_is_empty_response`), stall-after-content and sibling/domain failure — each asserting `calls.count("local") == 1`, no `"remote"` in `calls`, 429 with `X-Local-Route: refused` and the recorded reason token. These exits `continue` to the loop head where the choke point decides, so the row proves the structural guarantee rather than assuming it.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — a free-slot case: `local-preferred` + free local slot + admitting guard → served locally, no refusal (parent AC2).
- Comments/docstrings at every touched comparison site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (parent AC1) With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict on each listed exit path, no remote dispatch occurs (asserted per path in tests): pre-dispatch matrix rows assert `calls == []` and post-dispatch local-failure rows assert one local attempt only; every refusal is 429 with `X-Local-Route: refused` and its stable reason token (header and body agreeing), asserted per row with the row's own failure message.
- AC2 (parent AC2) With `local-preferred`, a free local slot and an admitting guard, the request is served locally: `calls == ["local"]`, 200, `X-Local-Route: local`, no 429.
- AC3 The pin decision has exactly one implementation: a test asserts both `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote` call sites and the admission-refusal path consult the same predicate, and that the predicate reads the canonical `admission_reserve` constants and `local_capacity_verdict()` (a spy/patch proves the helper is the only verdict source — no `if reason in (...)` table in `provider.py`).
- AC4 A `too_large` request is **never** refused by this path: the two size rows dispatch remote with `calls == ["remote"]` and 200, and no local-capacity 429 body is produced. (Chain-level stripping and the promoted log line belong to LP child "too-large promotion"; this AC pins only "no refusal".)
- AC5 (parent AC5) Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains: the existing matrix rows pass **unmodified**, and every anchored response keeps its headers/body apart from the additive `verdict` field delivered by LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6.
- AC6 (parent AC6) No queue-depth, lease or slot leak and no double header stamping on any of the above (asserted in tests): each refusal carries `X-Local-Route` exactly once and `contention_queue.queue_depth() == 0` after the request, with no lease left registered for the session.
- AC7 (parent AC7) Comments and docstrings updated at every touched comparison site and in the refusal builder; operator-facing docs (`proxy/docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) remain out of scope — tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC8 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (the changed-scope gate `/skill:test --scope changed` first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Never promote a fits-local request.** A `deferrable` request that cannot run now is refused/deferred, never silently moved to a paid provider (parent assumption A2).
- **Never refuse a too-large request** for local capacity; it falls through (parent AC4). Do not implement chain stripping here.

# Feature: deferral — queue-budget expiry yields a retryable 429

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP child "local-preferred pin across every local-route exit" (the pin predicate and the refusal path).

## Goal

A `local-preferred` request the verdict classifies `deferrable` waits in the existing contention queue, and when that wait budget (or the queue depth cap) is exhausted it gets a **retryable** 429 built by the truthful-timing helper — not a remote dispatch and not "All providers exhausted". The request is enqueued at most once, no lease or queue slot leaks, and the response is stamped once.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`, local dispatch gate ~:10824-:10905, the lease-active fallback ~:10713-:10756, and the lease path ~:11933):
  - Both contention-queue exits — `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` (wait budget expired) and the depth-cap exit (never enqueued) — are converted, for a pin-local + `deferrable` request, into a single refusal produced by `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` instead of falling through to the next provider.
  - The refusal reason is the existing canonical queue token `fallback_after_queue` (recorded through `_note_local_fallback_reason()` so the header and body agree); the timing stays entirely inside `_refusal_retry_timing()`, fed with the measured wait through `advertised_retry_after` (the queue's measured/remaining budget) so `Retry-After` / `retry_at` reflect the real wait rather than a re-derived estimate.
  - The refusal is returned **before** any remote candidate is resolved/dispatched and before any attempt/cooldown/usage-limit state is written, so nothing is enqueued twice and no lease is taken for a request that is being refused.
  - The lease-active fallback loop (~:10713, which currently walks to the next remote provider) must not run for a pin-local `deferrable` request; its refusal names `local_lease_active`.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — pin the two queue rows for `local-preferred` with explicit field assertions (`queue_wait_expiry`, `queue_depth_cap`).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` (or a focused addition) — queue-invariant assertions: enqueue-once, queue depth restored, no lease leak, single header stamp.
- Docstrings/comments on the converted branches: state that deferral ends in a retryable refusal and why (a fits-local request must never be promoted).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (parent AC3) With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict after the queue budget, the response is 429 with `retryable: true`, a `Retry-After`/`retry_at` pair consistent with the refusal timing contract (`retry_at` ≈ now + `Retry-After` within a small tolerance), `X-Local-Route: refused`, and a body verdict of `deferrable`; body `reason == "fallback_after_queue"` equals the `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` header.
- AC2 (parent AC3) The depth-cap exit (queue full, request never enqueued) produces the same retryable 429 shape and leaves the held waiter untouched (`contention_queue.queue_depth()` unchanged, 0 leaked).
- AC3 (parent AC1) With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict on each queue exit path, no remote dispatch occurs (asserted per path in tests): `calls == []` for both rows, and the response is not an exhaustion response (no `EXHAUSTION_*` code, no "All providers exhausted" text).
- AC4 (parent AC6) No queue-depth, lease or slot leak and no double header stamping on any of the above (asserted in tests): the request is enqueued at most once, `contention_queue.queue_depth()` returns to its pre-request value after the refusal, no local lease remains registered for the session, and `X-Local-Route` is stamped once — asserted on both queue exits and on the lease-active fallback.
- AC5 (parent AC6) Single stamping: the refusal is not re-stamped by the top-level `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (a patched stamp helper is never invoked with an already-stamped refusal).
- AC6 Truthful timing is preserved by construction: a test asserts the refusal's timing equals `_refusal_retry_timing("fallback_after_queue", advertised_retry_after=<measured remainder>)`, and the over-budget reasons still carry **no** `Retry-After` (existing `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` / `test_local_admission_guard.py` rows stay green unmodified).
- AC7 (parent AC5) Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains: they still fall through to the next provider after queue expiry exactly as today, and a remote-less (`private`) chain still defers and never promotes (parent assumption A5).
- AC8 (parent AC7) Comments and docstrings updated at every converted branch; operator-facing docs remain out of scope (LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57).
- AC9 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (changed-scope gate first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Queue bounds unchanged:** `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60 s) and `contention_queue_max_depth` keep their current values; no new config key or default.
- **No new queue implementation:** reuse `proxy/contention_queue.py` exactly as is (no priority promotion, no lease-grace tuning — that is LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R).
- **No timer renegotiation:** `_refusal_retry_timing()` owns `Retry-After` / `retry_at`; this slice only supplies an already-measured remainder through `advertised_retry_after`.
- **No promotion of a fits-local request** and no deferral of a too-large one (the latter is already stripped by LP child "too-large promotion").
- **Exactly one enqueue and one stamp**; a refusal must not leave attempt/cooldown state behind.
- No double refusal: the pin path (LP child C1) and this deferral path must not both build a response for the same request.

## Existing state (verified during planning)

- `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py` ~:7087-:7200) returns `("fallback", None, elapsed)` when `contention_queue.wait_for_local_slot()` returns `None` (caps exceeded), `("dispatch", None, elapsed)` when a slot frees, `("context_bypass", ...)` for size skips and `("refused_local_only", ...)` for the admission refusal. It stamps `request._local_queue_saturation` and `request._contention_queue_wait_seconds`.
- `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` handles the gate result around :10824-:10905: `contention_queue_dispatch` (queued and dispatched) and `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` (queued, budget expired → falls through to the next provider). The lease-active branch (~:10899) walks to the next remote provider.
- `contention_queue.wait_for_local_slot(max_wait_seconds, max_depth, slot_free_check, session_id, retained, eta_seconds, eta_ordering, promote_after_seconds)` returns `None` on cap exhaustion; `contention_queue.queue_depth()` exposes the current waiter count (used by existing tests).
- `_refusal_retry_timing(reason, eta_prefill_seconds=..., budget_seconds=..., projected_wait_seconds=..., advertised_retry_after=..., config=...)` (:4483) — `prefill_budget_exceeded` / `context_too_large` are in `NOT_TIME_RETRYABLE_REFUSAL_REASONS` (:4440); any other reason (including `fallback_after_queue`) keeps an ETA-derived timer with a 1 s floor and the `max_retry_after_seconds` cap, and honours `advertised_retry_after`.
- `_build_local_only_refusal_response(attempt, config)` (:~6530) builds the 429 from the attempt dict (`reason`, `eta_prefill_seconds`, `budget_seconds`, `projected_wait_seconds`) and stamps `X-Local-Route: refused`.
- Existing tests already cover the queue rows for `local-only` and `prefer-local`: `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py::_EXIT_ROWS` rows `queue_depth_cap` and `queue_wait_expiry`, with `_occupy_the_only_queue_slot()` seeding the depth cap and `contention_queue.reset()` in the autouse fixture.

## Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — queue-exit conversion in `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`, lease-active fallback, `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` call, `_note_local_fallback_reason()` for `fallback_after_queue`.
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — consumed only (`wait_for_local_slot()`, `queue_depth()`, `reset()`); no change.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — per-row retryable-429 assertions for the two queue exits.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — enqueue-once / no-leak / single-stamp invariants.

## Dependency graph (wired 2026-10-28)

- Depends on: LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 (local-preferred pin across every local-route exit).
- Depended on by: LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM (routing-outcome line).
- The too-large strip (LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4) is a sibling and does not overlap: that child removes the local entry before the queue is ever entered.

# Feature: too-large promotion — local stripped from the effective chain

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP child "local-preferred pin across every local-route exit" (pin predicate, verdict plumbing in both cycles).

## Goal

When the capacity verdict is `too_large`, the local route is not attempted at all: the local entry is removed from the effective chain at resolution time (the same structural filter `remote-ok` already uses), so the remote tiers serve the request with no local attempt, no queueing, no deferral and no local-capacity 429. A remote-less chain (e.g. `private`) is never stripped — it keeps deferring and never promotes (parent assumption A5).

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`:
  - Extend the chain filter so a `too_large` verdict removes every `type: local` entry — reuse the **existing** `remote-ok` comprehension rather than adding a second filter, e.g. `apply_local_preference(chain, preference, verdict=None)` treating `CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE` as "strip local". No new preference literal, no second chain-filter implementation.
  - Docstring states the two stripping reasons (`remote-ok` by preference, `too_large` by capacity) and the remote-less-chain carve-out.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (both cycles, `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` ~:9991 and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` ~:10664):
  - Compute the capacity verdict **once per request** before the dispatch loop, from the already-built `_RoutingEstimateCache` plus `server.local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (via `prefill_eta.COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY`) and the local entry's context ceiling, through `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)`; cache it on the request (e.g. `request._local_capacity_verdict`) so the refusal builder and the observability slice reuse it instead of recomputing.
  - Apply the verdict-aware filter to the cycle's chain before the `while True:` loop, so the local entry is never resolved, never queued and never refused. Guard the call so a chain with **no** non-local entry is left intact (empty-chain exhaustion must never be produced by stripping).
  - Stamp the outcome for the observability slice (`request._local_routing_outcome = "promoted"` / a shared constant), no separate log line here.
- Tests:
  - `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — a `local-preferred` + `too_large` row set: `calls == ["remote"]`, 200, no refusal code, `contention_queue.queue_depth() == 0`, and (with free local slots) the local dispatch stub never invoked.
  - `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — unit tests for the verdict-aware filter (strip on `too_large`, keep on `deferrable`, identical shape to `remote-ok`, remote-less chain untouched).
- Comments/docstrings at the filter and both cycle call sites.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (parent AC4) With `local-preferred` and a `too_large` verdict, the chain excludes local and a remote provider serves the request; no 429 is produced for local capacity (the local dispatch is never attempted, `calls == ["remote"]`, 200, nothing queued).
- AC2 The verdict is computed once per request before the dispatch loop and reused: a spy on `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict()` asserts one call per request per cycle and that the value is cached on the request for the refusal/observability paths.
- AC3 (parent A5, parent AC5) A remote-less chain (every entry `type: local`, e.g. `private`) is never stripped even when the verdict is `too_large`: the local route is still attempted and the existing deferral/refusal behaviour applies; no empty-chain "All providers exhausted" is produced by the filter.
- AC4 No second chain-filter implementation: a unit test asserts the verdict-stripped chain is identical to the `remote-ok`-stripped chain for the same input, and that `provider.py` introduces no new `type == "local"` filtering loop nor a new preference literal.
- AC5 (parent AC5) Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains, including when the verdict is `too_large` (existing `test_priority_routing.py` and matrix rows pass unmodified).
- AC6 (parent AC6) No queue-depth, lease or slot leak and no double header stamping on any of the above (asserted in tests): the promoted path engages no queue or lease (`contention_queue.queue_depth() == 0`, no lease registered), the request is dispatched exactly once, and one `X-Local-Route` header is stamped.
- AC7 (parent AC7) Comments and docstrings updated (filter + both cycle call sites); operator-facing docs remain out of scope (LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57).
- AC8 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (changed-scope gate first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Never promote a fits-local request:** only the `too_large` verdict strips local (parent assumption A2). Unclassifiable verdicts are `deferrable` (helper fail-safe) and stay pinned.
- **Never defer a too-large request:** stripping happens before the dispatch loop, i.e. before any queue entry.
- **Reuse, don't rebuild:** the existing `remote-ok` filter, `prefill_eta.COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY`, the existing routing estimate cache; no new estimator, no new sizing model (parent assumption A1).
- **Config defaults unchanged**, queue bounds unchanged.
- **No log line here** — the single per-request outcome line is LP child "routing-outcome line"; this slice only stamps the outcome.
- Scope guard: no `cached_ratio`/economic-bypass policy change, no contention-queue work (LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R).

## Existing state (verified during planning)

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py:410` `apply_local_preference(chain, preference)` — strips `type: local` entries only when `preference == "remote-ok"` (literal comparison removed by LP-0MVSHWVE005MS16); `:431` `effective_chain_for_request(request, model_config, server_config)` calls it. Both cycles call `effective_chain_for_request()` *before* the body has been read, which is why the verdict-aware strip cannot live inside the preference filter alone and must be applied by the cycle once the routing estimate exists.
- `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (`provider.py:9901`): chain resolution at :9991, `_raw_body = await request.body()` / `_routing_estimate = _RoutingEstimateCache(...)` at ~:10030-:10048, then `while True:` at ~:10053.
- `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (`provider.py:10572`): chain resolution at :10664, `body_json` and `_routing_estimate` built at ~:10640-:10700, then `while True:` at ~:10700.
- `_RoutingEstimateCache` (`provider.py`, used at both cycles) computes the authoritative routing estimate once per cycle — the input the verdict needs; `_provider_context_limit(provider_cfg)` (:3235) exposes the per-entry context ceiling (`max_context_tokens`), and `server.local_model_ctx_size` is the global local context cap.
- `prefill_eta.COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY = "local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens"` (`prefill_eta.py:209`); the shipped default is 25 000 (parent assumption A1).
- `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` (delivered by LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB) classifies `new_tokens > budget_tokens`, `prefill_budget_exceeded` and `context_too_large` as `too_large`; everything else, including unknown tokens, as `deferrable`.
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` (~430 lines) already tests `effective_chain_for_request()`; `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` rows `router_skip_physical_cap` (`context_too_large`) and `entry_context_cap` are the natural `too_large` fixtures.

## Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — verdict-aware chain filter reusing the `remote-ok` strip, docstring.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — pre-loop verdict computation and chain strip in both cycles, verdict caching on the request, outcome stamp.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — consumed only: `CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`, `local_capacity_verdict()`.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — consumed only: `COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY`.
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — filter unit tests (strip/keep/remote-less/`remote-ok` parity).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — end-to-end promoted-row assertions (remote only, no 429, no queue).

## Dependency graph (wired 2026-10-28)

- Depends on: LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 (local-preferred pin across every local-route exit).
- Depended on by: LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM (routing-outcome line).
- Sibling of record: LP-0MVSM06BK008FZUE (deferral) — that child handles the `deferrable` queue expiry; this child guarantees a `too_large` request never reaches it.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator reading the daily proxy usage report, I want the GPU busy-time
figure to reflect the *hardware's* actual compute activity (measured from GPU
power draw at 15-second resolution) rather than only the proxy's logged slot
occupancy, so I can tell how hard the GPU really worked and spot gaps between
proxy accounting and reality.

## Context

The report's `## Local model utilization` section computed "busy" entirely from
proxy logs (`aggregation.BusyStats`): it pairs `Stream started`/`Stream
finished` events, extends each back to its dispatch time, clips to the window
and unions the intervals. That measures *slot occupancy* — including queued
time and excluding GPU work the proxy did not log — not hardware utilisation.

On this Strix Halo APU `gpu_busy_percent` is pinned at 100% and is unusable
(LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP). Power draw is the discriminating signal; the
`gpu:computing:bool` recording rule (`power >= 90 W`) is evaluated by
Prometheus every 15 s from the node_exporter hwmon series
(`monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`).

## Change

Add a hardware-side, power-based GPU busy measurement alongside the log-based
figures:

- New module `gpu_busy.py` queries `avg_over_time(gpu:computing:bool[Nh])`
  (raw 15 s series) and the 5-minute-smoothed `gpu:power_watts:avg5m` trace.
- `reporting.run_analysis` populates `AnalysisResult.gpu_busy` best-effort
  (None if Prometheus is unreachable — the report never fails).
- The utilization table gains a `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` row, the
  `--json` summary gains a `gpu_busy` block, and the CLI text summary names
  the power-based figure.
- Docs: `SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` describe the method and the 15 s cadence.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` row appears in the `## Local model
   utilization` table with the power-based busy time and %, and is omitted
   (no crash) when Prometheus is unavailable.
2. `--json` exposes `gpu_busy` with `computing_fraction`, `busy_pct`,
   `busy_seconds`, `idle_seconds`, `total_seconds`, and the `smoothed_power`
   trace; `gpu_busy` is `null` when the query fails.
3. The computation uses `avg_over_time(gpu:computing:bool[Nh])` over the raw
   15-second series (not a down-sampled 1-minute pull of a smoothed series).
4. Unit tests cover: instant (`value`) and matrix (`values`) response formats,
   Prometheus-unreachable, empty result, invalid/out-of-range values,
   zero/negative window, JSON round-trip, and report row rendering.
5. `ruff check` is clean and the proxy-usage-analysis test suite passes.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_gpu_busy.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`

## Goal (user story)

As an operator reading the proxy usage report, I want the question "should GPU
utilisation come from `amd-smi` (or a tool like `amdtop`) instead of power
draw?" answered **once, with measured evidence, in the place I would look** —
so the power-based `gpu:computing:bool` measurement is not replaced by a
counter that saturates on this APU, and nobody re-litigates the decision.

## Answer (measured on this host, 2026-10-28)

**No — do not switch.** Two separate facts, both measured here:

1. `amd-smi` returns `N/A` for every metric the report needs on this
   `gfx1151` APU; `rocm-smi` and `amdtop` reach a value only by reading the
   **same** `gpu_busy_percent` sysfs counter this repo already samples.
2. That counter is **not a utilisation measure**: it latches to ~100 % as soon
   as the GPU draws more than ~20 W and only falls back at < 20 W. Over 7 days
   of Prometheus history it read ≥ 90 % for 93.8 % of samples while the GPU was
   at compute power (≥ 90 W) only 28.1 % of the time — i.e. **45 % false-busy**.

### amd-smi / rocm-smi / amdtop probes

| Probe | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GPU inventory | `amd-smi list` | one GPU, BDF `0000:c5:00.0` (the APU) |
| Engine usage | `amd-smi metric --usage`, `amd-smi monitor` | `USAGE: N/A`; `GFX% = N/A` |
| Power | `amd-smi metric --power`, `amd-smi monitor` | `SOCKET_POWER: N/A`, `POWER = N/A`, `PWR_CAP = N/A` |
| Clocks / thermals | `amd-smi metric --clock -t`, `amd-smi monitor` | `GFX_CLK: N/A`, `GPU_T/MEM_T: N/A` |
| Energy counter | `amd-smi metric --energy` | `energy: "N/A"` |
| Memory | `amd-smi monitor --json` | `vram_used 0.3 GB / vram_total 1.0 GB` — VRAM only; an APU serves from GTT, so this misdescribes the host |
| `rocm-smi` (same family) | `rocm-smi --showuse --showpower` | power `108 W` (same `hwmon` node), `GPU use 100%` (the `gpu_busy_percent` counter) |
| `amdtop` (Linux) | source: `linux.go:151` — `os.ReadFile(gpuDevPath + "/gpu_busy_percent")` (`zyoung11/amdtop` @ `5e500c3`) | "GPU usage" **is** `gpu_busy_percent`; power/temp come from the same `hwmon` `power1_average`/`temp1_input` the report uses; VRAM from `mem_info_vram_*` (not GTT). Windows uses ADLX, a Windows-only driver library — irrelevant here |
| Working alternative (already in use) | `hwmon5/power1_average` | 11–26 W idle, 91–120 W under decode/prefill — live and discriminating |
| No joule counter | `ls hwmon5/energy*` | absent, so no energy accumulator either |

`amdtop` therefore adds no new signal: it renders the same counter the pinned
`gpu_busy_percent` caveat already covers.

### Why the counter cannot be the utilisation figure (7-day evidence)

Prometheus has scraped `gpu_busy_percent` "for continuity only" since the
monitoring stack shipped, so the premise could finally be quantified instead of
asserted. Query: `gpu_busy_percent` vs `gpu:power_watts:amdgpu`, 5-min steps,
7 days to 2026-10-28 23:40 UTC (904 paired samples).

| GPU power band | samples | mean `gpu_busy_percent` | share ≥ 90 % |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–20 W | 44 | 2.3 % | 2 % |
| 20–40 W | 414 | 98.9 % | 99 % |
| 40–60 W | 90 | 100.0 % | 100 % |
| 60–80 W | 7 | 100.0 % | 100 % |
| 80–90 W | 96 | 100.0 % | 100 % |
| 90–100 W | 175 | 99.1 % | 98 % |
| 100–125 W | 78 | 95.7 % | 95 % |

It is a **bang-bang indicator that saturates at ~20 W**, not a graded
utilisation measure: once the GPU draws > 20 W it reads ~100 % no matter
whether that is 25 W (idle-with-resident-context) or 120 W (prefill). Summary
statistics: mean 94.5 % vs 28.1 % power-derived computing time; Pearson
`r(busy, power) = 0.28`; false-busy (`busy ≥ 90 %` ∧ `power < 40 W`) 45.2 % of
samples, longest continuous run **5.3 h**; false-idle (`busy < 90 %` ∧
`power ≥ 90 W`) 0.8 % — it never *under*-reports, which is why a short
observation (it does ramp 0 → 55 → 83 → 99 under load and decays afterwards)
looks convincing while an hour-scale view exposes the latch.

Consequence: the report's power-derived `gpu:computing:bool ≥ 90 W` figure
stays the discriminating hardware signal; `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` and `amdtop`
are all the same saturated counter (or `N/A`), and neither adds history — a
24 h window needs a time series, which the existing 10 s sysfs sampler →
node_exporter → Prometheus pipeline (90 d retention) already provides.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Why is GPU utilisation measured from power and not
  from AMD's own tool (or `amdtop`)?" — wants the documented, evidence-backed
  answer where the measurement is described (`monitoring/README.md`, the
  usage-analysis `REFERENCE.md`), not a restated assertion.
- **Agent working a usage/observability question (secondary).** Needs the
  decision pinned so it is not "improved" into an `amd-smi`/`amdtop` shell-out
  that would silently report a saturated number as utilisation.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-28)

| Capability | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Power-based GPU busy in the usage report | `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` (`avg_over_time(gpu:computing:bool[Nh])`), row `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` | Done (LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4) |
| Power recording rules | `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` (`gpu:power_watts:amdgpu`, `gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`) | Done (LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48) |
| Rationale "why not `gpu_busy_percent`" | rule-file header, `monitoring/README.md` §527, `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` §107, `REFERENCE.md`, `SKILL.md`, doc-guard test `test_documents_the_pinned_busy_counter_caveat` | Done — but worded as an unexplained **"pinned at 100 %"** assertion |
| Quantified characterisation of the counter (latch at ≥ 20 W, 45 % false-busy) | — | **Missing** (this item) |
| Rationale "why not `amd-smi` / `rocm-smi` / `amdtop`" | — | **Missing** (this item) |
| Guard preventing an `amd-smi`/`amdtop` shell-out | — | **Missing** (this item) |

## Desired change

Document the measured decision and pin it with a test — **no behaviour change**:

1. `monitoring/README.md`: replace the bare "pinned at 100 %" assertions (§202
   rationale, §273 series list, §527 troubleshooting) with the measured
   statement (bang-bang at ~20 W, 7-day figures, dated) and add a "Why not
   `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`" subsection carrying the condensed `N/A`
   table and the `amdtop` source finding.
2. `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` (§107 series table) and the header of
   `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`: same correction, keeping the "must not
   be used in a rule" wording intact.
3. `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` (§ GPU busy time from power)
   and `SKILL.md` (same section): one sentence each stating that `amd-smi`
   reports `N/A` and `amdtop`/`rocm-smi` just read the saturating
   `gpu_busy_percent`, cross-linking `monitoring/README.md`.
4. `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`: extend the doc-guard coverage
   (pattern: `test_documents_the_pinned_busy_counter_caveat`) so the docs must
   record the `amd-smi` `N/A` finding and the measured saturating behaviour,
   and assert `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` contains no
   `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi` subprocess call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The work item records the decision and its measured evidence: the `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi`/`amdtop` probe table (with the `amdtop` source line reference `linux.go:151`, commit `5e500c3`), the 7-day power-band table, and the two structural reasons (no history; same saturating counter) — each reproducible with the listed commands/queries.
- AC2: `monitoring/README.md` no longer asserts an unexplained "pinned at 100 %": every GPU-utilisation rationale there states the measured behaviour (latches to ~100 % above ~20 W; ≥ 90 % in 93.8 % of 7-day samples vs 28.1 % at compute power; 45 % false-busy) with the measurement date, and a "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`" subsection records that `amd-smi` is `N/A` on this APU and that `amdtop`/`rocm-smi` read only `gpu_busy_percent`, naming `hwmon` → Prometheus `gpu:computing:bool` as the retained source.
- AC3: `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` and the `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` header carry the same measured statement, and both keep an explicit prohibition on selecting `gpu_busy_percent` in any rule.
- AC4: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` § GPU busy time from power and `SKILL.md` § GPU busy time from power each state that `amd-smi` is not the source on this APU (`N/A`) and that `amdtop`-style tools only surface the saturating counter, cross-linking `monitoring/README.md`.

## Constraints

- **Documentation + guard tests only.** No new dependencies, no new sampler, no

  wedge-detector behaviour (its disable remains justified — the counter
  saturates at ≥ 20 W, so `gpu_busy_percent >= 90` fires while idle).
- Measured evidence must be reproducible offline; the guard test must not shell

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: doc rot.** Kernel 7.0.0-34 already changed the counter's behaviour
  relative to the 2026-07-31 "pinned from boot" observation (kernel 7.0.0-28),
  so the wording must be dated and phrased as a measurement with the query
  used, making a re-measure obvious. *Mitigation:* AC1/AC2 require the date and
  the commands; the 7-day analysis is repeatable from Prometheus history.
- **Risk: over-claiming.** The latch could be a sampling artefact of the
  textfile sampler. *Mitigation:* the band table uses 15 s scrapes (the sampler
  writes at 10 s) and the 5-min step samples the instant value, so the latch is
  the counter's own behaviour; AC2 cites the figures rather than a mechanism.
- **Risk: over-broad guard.** A source-text test could ossify the
  implementation. *Mitigation:* assert only the absence of an
  `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi`/`amdtop` shell-out in `gpu_busy.py`, not its structure.
- **Assumption (pending producer confirmation):** the desired outcome is to
  *record the measured decision*, not to build an alternative
  hardware-utilisation sampler. The remaining avenue
  (`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`, struct 264 B, format revision 3.0,
  populated and live — the interface that yields real GFX-activity
  accumulators) is filed as **LP-0MVSQT7YC0045HFW** rather than folded in here.
- **Assumption:** "medium" priority (operator-specified) — the current
  measurement is correct, so this is decision hygiene plus a documentation
  correction, not a defect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (operator, 2026-10-28):** "In the usage report skill we estimate GPU use by measuring power consumption. This is an AMD GPU and we can use the `amd-smi` CLI — should we switch to using that? (priority medium)." — **Answer:** researched on the live host: no. `amd-smi` 26.2.2 / ROCm 7.2.4 reports `N/A` for usage, socket power, clocks, thermals and energy on the single `gfx1151` device. Source: operator request + local measurement.
- **Q (operator, follow-up, 2026-10-28):** "The github project `amdtop` has GPU usage — check its source to see how it gets it (`https://github.com/zyoung11/amdtop`)." — **Answer:** cloned at `5e500c3`; Linux "GPU usage" is `gpu_busy_percent` read directly from sysfs (`linux.go:151`), power/temp from the same `hwmon` files, VRAM from `mem_info_vram_*` (not GTT); Windows uses ADLX. discovered-from:LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL

While evaluating `amd-smi` for GPU utilisation (LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` was found populated and live on this Strix Halo APU: 264 bytes, header `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` (`amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0`), with values changing between samples and plausible clocks (~1793 MHz) — i.e. the interface `amdgpu_top` uses to report real GFX/memory activity, as opposed to the pinned `gpu_busy_percent`.

Why it matters: the report's GPU busy time currently infers activity from power draw (`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot distinguish GFX work from any other power draw (e.g. memory-bound or idle-with-kernels cases). A real activity accumulator would be a direct measurement.

Scope (idea stage): decode the v3.0 struct layout from the kernel header, quantify whether the activity fields track compute vs idle, and decide whether to sample them into the existing node_exporter textfile pipeline. Overlaps LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (GPU telemetry sampler) — check that item before starting work.

Every temporal exit (cooldown, resident-prefix, thrash, queue cap/expiry, lease, quota, economic) does refuse via the loop-head choke point (`provider.py:6999`, called at `:10412` and `:11096`).
- **AC4 partial** — `routing_skip_provider_context` (`provider.py:3340-3347`) emits `session=` but no `preference=`, so the per-entry context-ceiling skip line is not attributable by preference.
- **AC6 partial** — `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py:649` inverts the required `local-only` ⇒ refusal half for the `context_too_large` / `entry_context_cap` rows (asserts 200 + remote dispatch).
- **AC3, AC5, AC7 met** — prefer-local parity, `preference=… session=…` on `priority_routing` in both cycles, and the routing.md section are in place.

## Question for the producer (this blocks the verdict)

AC1 enumerates `context_too_large` and the per-entry context cap as exits that must refuse under `local-only`, but the implementation intentionally does not pin `too_large`; the code comment attributes that to LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4 "parent AC4" (waiting cannot help, so the request must fall through to remote and must not be refused for local capacity). 1. **AC1 as written** — pin/refuse the `too_large` exits as well, and add `preference=` to the context-skip line; or
